caption: The public pricing page of Shiftie, shiftie.co/pricing, with the heading How much will it cost me?, the line All plans come with a free 28-day trial, the checks No card details required and Free 7-day UK-based support, the slider set to 1 Employees, and the Monthly Plan card at £2.75 per month with the button START FREE TRIAL, next to the list What's Included (Employee Scheduling, Availability, HR Management, Leave, Documents, Time Clock & Timesheets, Multi Venue). The page is in English. No personal data is shown.

The Team page inside the app (Team (6)) under the bar You have 28 days left on your trial with the button Add Billing Details: the Employees tab with the five test employees in the list, each with the orange note No Email, the default job role Management and weekly hours 0. The row of the account owner and the avatar at the bottom left are covered by black boxes that the tester drew; they were checked and no name, e-mail address or avatar is readable.

The Schedule page for the week Mon 23 Nov to Sun 29 Nov: the group Other Employees with 25 Shifts - 200h 0m, and the shift cards of four of the five test employees (09:00 - 17:00, 12:00 - 20:00, 07:00 - 15:00 and 10:00 - 18:00, Monday to Friday) with the job role Management and a break of 0m, and below the weekly total of 200h 0m and costs of £ 0,00 because no pay rate was set. The schedule name on each of the 20 visible shift cards is covered by a box; the row of the account owner and the avatar at the bottom left were covered black by the tester and were checked.

The window PUBLISH SHIFTS FOR Mon 23 Nov - Sun 29 Nov, opened with the button Publish 25 Shifts, with the fields Employees (All Employees and All Open Shifts), Groups, Job Roles and Tags and the button Publish 25 Shifts. The window says nothing about e-mail or text messages, and the button was not clicked. The schedule name in the schedule picker at the top left and on the 10 shift cards that show it below the window is covered by a box; the row of the account owner and the avatar at the bottom left were covered black by the tester and were checked.
